scope: Irregularities found while building the NFL line-origination section. The pre-existing dashboard keeps its own list (IR-001..IR-021) on the root Flagged for Review page; this page does not restate or delete those.
rule: A flag is published, never resolved by deletion. Items here do not block merge or deploy; they block the conclusions they touch, and the blocked conclusion stays blank on the page it belongs to.

items.title: No official NFL Next Gen Stats download repository exists at the address tutorials cite
items.detail: The GitHub REST API returns 404 'Not Found' for the repository 'NFL/Next-Gen-Stats', which a number of third-party write-ups present as the place to download official weekly tracking CSVs. A GitHub repository search for that name returns only third-party scrapers, one of which describes itself as 'Weekly data scraped from NFL Next Gen Stats website'.
items.effect: Any plan that assumed free bulk official tracking data must instead assume either a subscription product or a scraping pipeline with its own terms-of-service exposure. LM-07 is blocked on this, and the site does not promise snap-share history.
items.action: Keep Q-11 open; if a tracking feed is ever bought, store it with the same raw-response-plus-hash discipline as the schedule data.

items.title: The league site has no working per-team depth-chart or transactions page at the expected paths
items.detail: Both https://www.nfl.com/teams/san-francisco-49ers/depth-chart and the transactions path returned the site's 404 page during this session, while the club's own page (49ers.com/team/depth-chart) is live, dated and complete.
items.effect: Depth and roster-move ingestion must be built as 32 club-specific parsers with per-club staleness checks, which is a maintenance commitment, not a one-time task (SG-10). Any claim of 'league-wide availability tracking' must state that it is 32 separate club publications.
items.action: Collector records HTTP status, the club's own 'Updated as of' date and a row count per club; a club that returns fewer rows than its recent median raises a flag instead of publishing a quiet blank.

items.title: The official roster-rules source found is written around the 2022 offseason
items.detail: The league's roster FAQ describing the injured-repository four-game minimum, the eight designated-return cap, the PUP/NFI windows and the 16-man practice squad is current as of its own publication date, and its dates and examples are 2022. Roster rules are renegotiated between seasons.
items.effect: Every availability window computed from these rules carries a 'rule version' field, and LM-02 cannot be certified for 2026 until the current text is stored. No row on this site states a roster rule as a 2026 fact.
items.action: Q-09 stays open until the current-year rules are snapshotted into the repository with a hash.

items.title: Four documents that several rows depend on could not be retrieved this session
items.detail: The retrieval proxy returned a signature error for the New Jersey press-release pages containing the completed-events and bet-type tables, for the operator house-rules PDF, for the Indiana rule PDF, and for the full text of the arXiv paper (its abstract page was retrieved fine).
items.effect: Those rows are labelled PARTIAL or left blank (M-07 is blank, M-16 and M-17 are PARTIAL) and the conclusions that would have used them - parlay hold as a cost model, and the exact wording of correlation-void rules - are gated rather than assumed.
items.action: Re-run the collector for these four URLs; the verifier treats a PARTIAL source as ineligible to back a VERIFIED row.

items.title: Inherited schedule snapshot is 11 days old and incomplete in known ways
items.detail: The repository's official snapshot was captured 2026-11-02. It carries 272 regular-season matchup rows of which 24 have TBD kickoff times, and 49 preseason matchups with no dates; nothing released after 2026-11-02 is in it.
items.effect: Denominators for 'eligible slots' (gate G-14) and for rest-day features (ST-08) must be computed on a stated cut of the snapshot, not on the live league view.
items.action: Run the refresh collector, then restate the snapshot date on the header of each table that uses it (already shown per-dataset by SG-18).

items.title: The official report carries no diagnosis and only the latest practice status
items.detail: In the fetched 49ers block, the Injuries column is blank for all twelve listed players and the page shows one practice status rather than a Wednesday-to-Friday ladder, while the 'Injuries' column is populated for some players on other clubs' blocks.
items.effect: Severity, mechanism and multi-day participation trends cannot be modelled from this page alone, so no 'severity-weighted' feature is published; a third-party page that does carry those fields is deliberately excluded from value columns (Q-14).
items.action: Capture the report on every official report day so the ladder is built from successive snapshots rather than expected from one page.

items.title: A partially rendered official page is indistinguishable from a quiet week
items.detail: The retrieval proxy returned an unsupported-browser notice alongside usable content on the league pages, and returned a 'page is incomplete' notice when a club news path was probed. If a collector trusts any 200 response, a truncated render would look like 'no players listed', i.e. a healthy roster.
items.effect: This is the highest-risk failure mode for an automated pipeline in this domain, because it fails silently and in the direction of plausible-looking data.
items.action: The collector must assert per-club row counts and per-game block presence before accepting a snapshot, and the verifier must treat an unasserted count as a gate failure (SG-09 option A's stated risk, made mandatory).

items.title: Coverage is one club of thirty-two, and the extra blocks were not transcribed
items.detail: Structured injury data exists here for the San Francisco 49ers plus the opponent block on the same page. Roughly twenty further clubs appear inside the fetched chunks; their rows were read but deliberately not transcribed, because partial chunks cannot be certified as the full report for those clubs.
items.effect: The injuries page states its coverage explicitly rather than implying league-wide tracking. No cross-league aggregate (counts of DNPs by week, positional scarcity league-wide) is published anywhere on this site.
items.action: Fill by running the collector for all clubs and all report days of the season; then re-open the aggregate tables.

items.title: There is no market-price data anywhere in this repository
items.detail: No opening, midweek or closing price for any NFL market is stored here, and none is reachable from the build environment. Consequently: no edge, no CLV, no ROI, no correlation estimate, and no validated strategy exists in this section.
items.effect: Every result column is blank by rule. This is the item that converts the brief from 'build a model' into 'buy the one input you cannot synthesise', and it is why SG-01 is ranked first.
items.action: Owner decision on a price feed trial (Q-01); then LM-10, LM-12 and the leaderboard become computable.

items.title: Depth-chart 'vacancy' counts are normal at several positions and must not be read as weakness
items.detail: In the fetched chart, right guard, right tackle, fullback, nickel back, punter, kicker, holder and long snapper each list one player, and nine more positions list two. Single-name entries are how these roles are usually charted.
items.effect: A raw 'fewer than three names' metric would flag almost every team every week and carry no information, so no deficiency index is published until a league-wide baseline exists (SG-10).
items.action: Publish the count, not the verdict, and set the threshold only after 32-club collection provides the distribution.

items.title: The report and the depth chart describe different populations
items.detail: Two players listed on the 49ers' Week 10 report (a cornerback and a defensive tackle) do not appear anywhere on the fetched depth chart, while chart players appear on the report only when they are listed.
items.effect: Signals built by joining the two must treat 'in report, not on chart' and 'on chart, not in report' as first-class states; an inner join would silently drop availability evidence, and a left join from the chart would invent health.
items.action: Keep both as explicit coded states in the schema; add a unit test for the join semantics (already listed in R-04's acceptance criteria).

items.title: A blank game status is a meaningful state and is easy to mis-parse into signal
items.detail: The fetched 49ers block lists twelve players with no game-status designation at all. League policy explains it: a player certain to play is not listed, and the Probable category was abolished because about 95% of Probable players played.
items.effect: A parser that defaults a blank to 'Questionable', or that infers availability from the absence of a name, manufactures a signal out of a formatting convention - exactly the luck-as-skill failure the gates exist to stop.
items.action: Store blanks as the coded value NO_DESIGNATION; a unit test asserts that no numeric feature reads a blank as a probability.

items.title: Suggestions that require an owner decision were not implemented, and one that could have been was
items.detail: Nineteen of the twenty suggestions on the suggestions page are marked AWAITING-DECISION and changed nothing. Three were marked AUTO-DONE because they needed no decision, no money and no legal judgement: gate-enforced disclosures, per-dataset staleness stamps, and the decision-surfacing count on the section landing page.
items.effect: Nothing in this section should be read as an approved plan of work; it is a decision menu with costs attached.
items.action: Owner records choices (SG-03 proposes the decisions log); each accepted item then becomes a scoped task on the shared board.

items.title: Repeated retrievals of the same official page returned different row counts
items.what: The Week 10, 2026 league injury page was fetched four times in one session and returned 30 player rows, then 162 rows, then no rows at all, for the same URL and the same report.
items.why: Row count is the only cheap signal that a capture is complete, and here it is unstable by a factor of five. A larger capture is not automatically better: the 162-row variant could not be re-derived, so certifying its rows would rest on a single unverifiable read.
items.action: injuries.json publishes only the 30 rows that were present in a stored, quotable retrieval and whose per-club grouping is visible in the same chunk. The 162-row capture is recorded here and deliberately NOT published. The collector's render-integrity assertion (SG-09) plus the manifest's SHA-256 per capture are what make this class of discrepancy auditable instead of anecdotal.
